Choosing among the best UK universities for English is not simply a matter of selecting the most famous name. English can mean English Literature, English Language and Literature, creative writing, linguistics, literary theory or cultural studies.

For 2027 entry, applicants should compare the course itself as carefully as the university’s position in a league table. Oxford may suit someone who wants broad historical and language study, while Warwick may be a better fit for a student interested in contemporary theory and culture. Students who want a major literary city may prefer Edinburgh, UCL or King’s College London.

This guide compares the best UK universities for English in 2027 by academic strength, course structure, module choice, teaching style, location, cost and suitability for international students.

Quick answer: which are the best UK universities for English?

The strongest overall options include:

  1. University of Oxford
  2. University of Cambridge
  3. University of St Andrews
  4. Durham University
  5. University College London
  6. University of Edinburgh
  7. University of Warwick
  8. King’s College London
  9. University of Exeter
  10. University of York

Other universities worth considering include Bristol, Manchester, Glasgow, Leeds, Sheffield, Lancaster and the University of East Anglia.

There is no single best university for every applicant. The right choice depends on whether you want traditional English Literature, English Language and Literature, creative writing, literary theory, a London-based course or a smaller university environment.

What does English mean at a UK university?

Before comparing universities, decide which type of English degree you want.

An English Literature degree usually focuses on poetry, novels, drama, literary history, criticism and theory.

An English Language and Literature degree adds the study of language itself. This may include the development of English, linguistics, language variation, grammar and the relationship between language and culture.

An English Studies degree may combine literature with media, cultural studies, creative writing and communication.

For example, a student who enjoys Shakespeare, poetry and close textual analysis may prefer English Literature. Someone interested in how language changes across history and society may prefer English Language and Literature.

That distinction matters because two universities may use similar course titles but offer very different modules and assessment methods.

How we selected these universities

This shortlist combines subject rankings, official course information, module breadth, teaching style, academic reputation and student fit.

Different league tables measure different things. The Guardian places considerable emphasis on teaching, student satisfaction, feedback and graduate outcomes. QS focuses more strongly on international academic reputation and research. The Complete University Guide provides a UK-focused comparison by subject.

Use rankings as a starting point, then compare:

  • Course modules
  • Teaching and supervision
  • Assessment methods
  • Optional subjects
  • Research strengths
  • Entry requirements
  • Tuition fees
  • Living costs
  • International student support

A university with a higher position in one table is not automatically the best option for your interests.

1. University of Oxford

The University of Oxford remains one of the best universities for English if you want a demanding course with broad historical and linguistic coverage.

Its English Language and Literature course covers writing in English from the Anglo-Saxon period to the present day. Students may study poetry, drama, prose, literary criticism, language history and literature from different parts of the world.

Oxford is particularly suitable for students who enjoy independent reading, close discussion and intensive academic supervision. Tutorials require careful preparation, strong essay writing and the ability to defend an interpretation.

It is a strong choice for literary history, language study, postgraduate preparation and academic research. Applicants should check the official Oxford English course information for current requirements and assessment details.

Oxford is extremely competitive. Meeting the published minimum requirement does not guarantee an offer.

2. University of Cambridge

Cambridge is one of the top English Literature universities in the UK and is especially well known for literary history, close reading and specialist study.

The course covers major periods from medieval writing to contemporary literature. Students normally begin with broad study before choosing areas that match their interests. Depending on the available modules, options may include Renaissance literature, modernism, world literature, literary theory, American writing and film.

Cambridge suits applicants who enjoy detailed textual analysis, academic discussion and independent research. The supervision system gives students the opportunity to discuss essays and ideas in small groups.

Oxford and Cambridge are not identical. Oxford may appeal more to students who want a broader combination of language and literature, while Cambridge may suit students who prefer a strongly literary route with structured historical coverage. The Cambridge English course page should be checked for the latest 2027 details.

3. University of St Andrews

St Andrews is one of the top English study programmes in the UK for students who want a four-year Scottish degree and a close academic community.

The course can include medieval texts, Old English, Older Scots, poetry, prose, drama and contemporary writing. The Scottish degree structure gives students more time to explore related subjects before specialising.

St Andrews is a good option for students who want traditional literary study in a smaller university town. It offers a strong academic reputation without the scale and cost of London.

Students who value a close-knit environment, historical literature and a strong sense of university community should examine the St Andrews English course structure.

4. Durham University

Durham is a strong choice for English Literature, particularly for students who want historical depth and a collegiate university experience.

The department covers literature from the early medieval period to the present and includes writing from different parts of the English-speaking world. Students can normally choose optional modules as they progress through the degree.

Durham suits applicants who want a traditional English degree with room for modern and global approaches. The collegiate system can also provide academic and social support outside the department.

Before applying, compare the current module list with your interests. A course may carry the same title as another degree but offer a very different balance of theory, creative writing and literary history. The Durham English degree page provides the latest course information.

5. University College London

UCL is one of the best English universities in the UK for students who want to study in London while combining literature, language and culture.

Its English course covers literature across historical periods and may include language-related study, criticism and interdisciplinary options. Students also benefit from access to museums, theatres, publishers, archives and literary events.

UCL is particularly suitable for applicants interested in English Language and Literature rather than a purely traditional literature degree. Its London setting can also help students explore careers in publishing, communications, media and education.

London is expensive. Accommodation, transport and daily costs can be considerably higher than in York, Durham, Exeter or St Andrews. Compare the full annual budget before accepting an offer. Check the UCL English BA course details.

6. University of Edinburgh

Edinburgh is one of the best universities for English Literature for students who want to study in a major literary city.

The University of Edinburgh has a long-established department covering English and Scottish Literature. Its location provides access to festivals, theatres, archives, libraries and public literary events.

Edinburgh offers a four-year Scottish degree and a broad academic environment. It suits students who want literary study connected to a wider cultural life.

A student who attends readings, theatre performances and literary festivals may develop a different understanding of literature from someone whose experience remains entirely classroom-based. Prospective applicants should review the University of Edinburgh English Literature programme.

7. University of Warwick

Warwick is one of the best English universities in the UK for students who want contemporary theory and flexible study.

The department’s teaching can engage with gender, identity, diversity, ecology, culture and modern critical debates. Students who want an English degree beyond a fixed traditional canon may find Warwick especially attractive.

Warwick suits applicants interested in literary theory, cultural studies, modern literature and interdisciplinary work.

A less traditional course can sometimes provide greater academic freedom. Module flexibility may matter more than a small difference in league-table position if you already know the subjects you want to study. See the University of Warwick English course information.

8. King’s College London

King’s College London offers English study in the centre of one of the world’s major cultural cities.

The course combines historical study, close textual analysis and literary theory. Depending on the available modules, students may also work with archives, theatre, cultural organisations and London’s literary history.

King’s is a strong choice for students interested in publishing, journalism, theatre, media, cultural policy and communications.

Its central location is a major advantage, but living costs are high. Students should prepare a realistic budget for rent, transport, food and study materials. The King’s English BA course page should be checked before applying.

9. University of Exeter

Exeter offers a broad English degree with options that may include medieval literature, modern writing, film, creative writing and criticism.

It suits students who want a strong literary foundation but also want to explore subjects beyond the traditional canon. The campus environment can appeal to applicants who prefer a defined university community.

Exeter may be particularly useful for students who want to combine English Literature with creative or visual forms of storytelling. Check the available modules because optional subjects can change between academic years.

10. University of York

York is a strong option for applicants who want academic breadth with a supportive learning environment.

The course covers literature across historical periods, genres and critical approaches. Students can develop skills in close reading, research, essay writing and academic argument.

York suits students who want a respected English department in a manageable student city. It offers a balance between academic rigour and approachable teaching.

It may be a sensible alternative for applicants who want a leading English course but are looking beyond Oxford and Cambridge.

Best universities for English Literature

For traditional literary study, the strongest choices include:

  • Oxford
  • Cambridge
  • St Andrews
  • Durham
  • Edinburgh
  • York
  • Exeter
  • Bristol
  • Manchester
  • Glasgow

Oxford and Cambridge offer academic intensity and prestige. St Andrews and Durham provide historical depth. Edinburgh offers a literary-city experience, while York, Exeter, Bristol and Manchester provide broader choices in literature, culture and modern criticism.

Best English Language and Literature universities

Students who want language study alongside literature should consider:

  • Oxford
  • UCL
  • Cambridge
  • Edinburgh
  • King’s College London
  • Warwick

Important related entities include linguistics, language variation, grammar, historical language development, discourse and literary language. These subjects may appear in different proportions depending on the university.

English university rankings: how to compare them

There is no single ranking that measures everything an English applicant needs.

Use several sources together. A department may rank highly for research but offer fewer modules in your preferred area. Another may have stronger student satisfaction or a more suitable teaching structure.

Entry requirements for 2027

Entry requirements vary by university, qualification and applicant background. Many selective English degrees ask for excellent A-level or equivalent results. Some prefer English Literature, while others accept English Language and Literature or related subjects.

International applicants should check:

  • Accepted qualifications
  • Required grades
  • IELTS or other English-language scores
  • Subject requirements
  • Foundation-year options
  • Portfolio requirements for creative writing
  • Admissions assessments
  • Application deadlines

An IELTS score around 6.5 or 7.0 is common for many UK degrees, but selective courses may require higher individual component scores. Always confirm the current requirement on the relevant course page. Students comparing language conditions can also review guidance on English requirements for UK universities.

Undergraduate applications normally go through UCAS. Oxford and Cambridge usually have earlier deadlines than most other courses. Check the latest UCAS application dates before submitting an application.

Students unfamiliar with the process can use practical guidance on preparing a UK university application.

Tuition fees and living costs

Home fees and international fees are different. International tuition fees for leading English degrees may be approximately £22,000 to £35,000 per year, depending on the university and course.

A realistic annual budget may include:

  • Tuition: £22,000 to £35,000
  • Living outside London: approximately £10,000 to £18,000
  • Living in London: approximately £15,000 to £22,000 or more
  • Books, travel and personal costs: approximately £1,000 to £3,000

How to choose the right English degree

Start with the course rather than the university name.

Ask yourself:

  1. Do I want English Literature or English Language and Literature?
  2. Do I prefer traditional literary history or modern theory?
  3. Do I want creative writing, film or cultural studies?
  4. Would I prefer London or a smaller university city?
  5. Can I afford the location?
  6. Are the entry requirements realistic?
  7. Does the department offer the modules I actually want?
  8. Do I want a dissertation or research-led final year?

Someone interested in Renaissance drama should not choose only by overall reputation. The better question is whether the department offers the right modules, teaching expertise and academic resources.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best university for English in the UK?

Oxford and Cambridge are leading choices for prestige and academic intensity. St Andrews, Durham, UCL, Edinburgh, Warwick, King’s, Exeter and York may be better depending on course preference, budget and location.

Which are the best UK universities for English Literature?

Oxford, Cambridge, St Andrews, Durham, Edinburgh and York are particularly strong. Warwick and King’s are excellent for applicants who prefer theory and interdisciplinary study.

Is Oxford or Cambridge better for English?

Neither is automatically better. Oxford may suit students seeking broad English Language and Literature study, while Cambridge may suit those who prefer a strongly literary course with later specialisation.

Which universities are best for English Language and Literature?

Oxford, UCL, Cambridge, Edinburgh, King’s and Warwick are strong choices. Compare modules carefully because the balance between language, linguistics and literature varies.

Are rankings enough to choose an English degree?

No. Rankings help create a shortlist, but modules, assessment, teaching, location, fees and student support should influence the final decision.

Can international students apply for 2027 entry?

Yes. International applicants can apply through UCAS, provided they meet the university’s qualification, English-language and deadline requirements.

Is London a good place to study English?

London offers access to publishers, theatres, archives, museums and literary events. It is also one of the most expensive student locations in the UK, so applicants should plan the full cost before accepting an offer.

Final advice

The best UK universities for English do not all offer the same experience. Oxford and Cambridge provide exceptional academic intensity. St Andrews and Durham suit students who prefer traditional literary study. UCL and King’s connect English with London’s cultural life. Edinburgh offers a strong literary setting, while Warwick, Exeter and York provide different combinations of flexibility, theory and student support.

For 2027 entry, compare the actual modules, entry requirements, tuition fees, living costs and application deadline before making a decision. The university’s reputation matters, but the course you will study for three or four years matters more.
